_about: Settings → Connectors → Discover: the connectors Yap can use today (8 Nov 2026), from the official servers' public addresses. Only ones that let any app sign in by itself (dynamic client registration), or take a pasted token, or run on this PC. `tested` is the date someone signed in and ran its tools with Yap (shown as Tested with Yap); null until then. catalog.rs reads it; docs/architecture/integrations.md, "The catalogue".

connectors.name: Notion
connectors.blurb: Search, read and write the pages and databases in your Notion workspace.
connectors.notes: An Enterprise workspace's admin may allow only the apps they've approved.

connectors.name: Linear
connectors.blurb: Find, create and update issues, projects and comments.

token.help: A personal API key from Linear's settings works too, instead of signing in.

connectors.name: Atlassian
connectors.blurb: Search and update Jira issues and Confluence pages.
connectors.notes: Your site's admin may need to allow it first.

connectors.name: GitHub
connectors.blurb: Repositories, issues, pull requests and code search.

token.help: Make a fine-grained personal access token with read access to the repositories you want, then paste it here.

connectors.notes: GitHub doesn't let other apps sign in to it this way yet, so it takes a token.

connectors.name: Supabase
connectors.blurb: Look into your Supabase projects: tables, queries, logs and settings.

token.help: A personal access token from your Supabase account works too, instead of signing in.

connectors.notes: Added read-only: Chat can look but not change anything. For changes, add it by hand without read_only=true.

connectors.name: Sentry
connectors.blurb: Errors, issues and releases, and what caused them.

connectors.name: Cloudflare
connectors.blurb: Your Cloudflare account: Workers, DNS, logs and more.

token.help: A Cloudflare API token works too, instead of signing in.

connectors.name: Airtable
connectors.blurb: Read and update the records in your Airtable bases.

token.help: An Airtable personal access token works too, instead of signing in.

connectors.name: Intercom
connectors.blurb: Search conversations, contacts and help articles.
connectors.notes: For workspaces hosted in the US. Intercom has another address for EU ones.

connectors.name: Granola
connectors.blurb: Your Granola meeting notes, for Chat to search and read.
connectors.notes: Off by default on Granola's Enterprise plan: its admin turns it on.

connectors.name: Fireflies
connectors.blurb: Your Fireflies meeting transcripts and summaries.

token.help: A Fireflies API key works too, instead of signing in.

connectors.name: Stripe
connectors.blurb: Customers, payments, invoices and subscriptions, and Stripe's docs.

token.help: A restricted API key works too, instead of signing in. Start with a sandbox's.

connectors.notes: It can move money: try it with a sandbox account first. Its refund, payment link and invoice tools start Off.

connectors.name: Zapier
connectors.blurb: The actions you set up in Zapier, across the apps it connects.

token.help: Zapier gives apps it doesn't list a connection token: copy it from your Zapier MCP server's page, then paste it here.

connectors.name: Home Assistant
connectors.blurb: The lights, switches and other devices in your home.

token.help: Make a long-lived access token: your Home Assistant profile → Security → Long-lived access tokens.

connectors.notes: Turn on Home Assistant's Model Context Protocol Server integration first. It's on your network, so nothing goes over the internet.

connectors.name: Files
connectors.blurb: Read and write the files in folders you choose, on this PC.
connectors.notes: A program on this PC. Add each folder it may use after the other arguments.

later.name: Google Workspace
later.blurb: Gmail, Drive, Calendar, Docs and Sheets.
later.why: Google's servers are a preview that needs an app Google has reviewed, and Gmail and Drive need its security review too. Your Google Calendar already works in Yap, above.

later.name: Microsoft 365
later.why: Microsoft's needs each organisation's admin to approve Yap, and a paid Copilot plan.

later.name: Slack
later.why: Slack lets only apps listed in its Marketplace sign in, and Yap isn't listed yet.

later.name: Figma
later.why: Figma lets only the apps on its own list sign in, and it isn't adding new ones for now.
